newsitem.title: USA: Calif. Senate OKs bill to alter L.A. transit board.
newsitem.headline: Calif. Senate OKs bill to alter L.A. transit board.

text.p: California's Senate on Wednesday approved a bill that would change the way the financially-troubled Los Angeles County Metropolitan Transportation Authority is governed.
The Senate approved Senate Bill 567 on a vote 32-to-2, sending it to the state Assembly for review.

Under existing state law, the Los Angeles County Metropolitan Transportation Authority's governing board is comprised of 14 members, including five members of the Los Angeles County Board of Supervisors, the mayor of Los Angeles, three members appointed by the mayor, four members appointed by the Los Angeles County-City Selection Committee, and one non-voting member named by the governor.

Under Senate Bill 567, by Senator Richard Polanco, the authority's board would consist of 12 members, including two members of the county Board of Supervisors, the mayor of Los Angeles, one member appointed by the mayor, two members appointed by the city council, five members appointed by the Los Angeles County-City Selection Committee, and one non-voting member appointed by the governor.
